newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota hospital searches for conduit issuer.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota hospital searches for conduit issuer.

text.p: A Minnesota health care system is searching for a conduit issuer for $175 million of tax-exempt bonds after a Minneapolis City Council committee turned thumbs down on the issue this week.
Fairview Health System had asked the city for the bond issue, which would mainly fund the system's acquisition of University of Minnesota Hospital, according to Jean Tracy, a Fairview spokeswoman.

However, the city council's development committee rejected the request due to pressure from the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees, which lost its representation of hospital workers when Fairview acquired the hospital in Janauary, Tracy said.
That dispute is currently before the National Labor Relations Board, she said. Meanwhile, Fairview has begun to take steps to find another conduit issuer.
Dave Finn, Fairview's director of capital structure, said the Minnesota Agricultural and Economic Development Board has agreed to look at the bond plan.

He said the size and scope of the deal would be unusual for the board, pointing out that Minnesota, unlike many other states, lacks a state agency charged specifically with issuing debt for health care-related projects. Instead, most hospital deals are done through the city government where the project is located.
The bonds, which Fairview plans to insure with MBIA Insurance Corp., have earned an A-plus rating from Standard & Poor's Corp. and an A1 rating from Moody's Investors Service, according to Finn.

Finn said in the past Fairview has issued its debt through Minneapolis. He said if the state board does not issue the debt, which would be underwritten by Smith Barney Inc., the health care system would look to issue about $54 million of the bonds not related to the University of Minnesota Hospital acquisition through the city of Edina and the rest on its own on a taxable basis.
The taxable portion would probably be privately placed as notes with the hope that Minneapolis would change its mind about participating in the deal and ultimately sell tax-exempt bonds, Finn said.

He said Fairview must come up with $87.5 million to pay off a promissory note it issued for the university hospital. That note expires June 30. Another $23 million of the $175 million bond issue would be for capital improvements at the hospital.
